focus_area_title: Improve Communication and Access to Senior Leaders
content_text_body:
Employees who have access to key decision makers tend to trust their company more. The goal is to bridge communication and connection between your team and senior leaders so that everyone understands each other better.

### Collect and share stories

Look for examples of leaders' actions that show their personal side and convey the right company values.  

Do the same with your team. Capture stories where the team has overcome big challenges, worked together to pull off the impossible, and learned or built confidence from failures.

Share positive stories about senior leaders with your team and vice versa. This will help each group understand the other and feel a sense of shared success.

### Be an Effective Advocate

To be an advocate for your team, you must understand each team member's experiences and needs and seek out the appropriate support for them.  

Practice asking your team members how they are doing, if they need any support, and what concerns they have about the business. Ask them to help you build a case for a new approach or idea to improve team and business performance.  

Make a commitment to pass along their ideas and concerns to senior leaders. Be specific about when and how you will do that, and how you will keep them informed.  

### Encourage Opportunities for Access to Senior Leaders

Look for ways to give your team members more access to senior leaders. For example, invite a guest leader to your team meeting, encourage skip-level 1:1s, and suggest open forums or townhalls. Leave the agenda open and light - e.g., business update  from the leader, followed by Q&A opportunity for team members - allowing for an authentic, two-way conversation.
